words.enDefinition: to tell new people your name and basic information

examples.en: Our orientation leader asked everyone to introduce yourself to the person beside them.
examples.zh: 迎新带队的同学请大家向旁边的人「自我介绍」。

examples.en: You can introduce yourself with just your name if the group is large.
examples.zh: 如果人很多，你可以只报个名字来「自我介绍」。

collocations: briefly introduce yourself
introduce yourself to the group
take turns to introduce yourself

words.enDefinition: offers to help two people meet for the first time

examples.en: I said "Let me introduce you to my neighbour" when my classmate joined us.
examples.zh: 同学走过来时，我说：「我来介绍你们认识」，这是我的邻居。

examples.en: When we reached the table, Mei said "Let me introduce you to my lab partner."
examples.zh: 走到桌边时，阿梅说：「我来介绍你们认识」，这是我的实验搭档。

collocations: let me introduce you to my roommate
let me introduce you to the others
come over and let me introduce you

words.enDefinition: to present a newcomer to several people who are together

examples.en: It helps to introduce someone to the group before everyone splits off into smaller conversations.
examples.zh: 大家分头聊天前，「把新来的人介绍给大家」会有帮助。

examples.en: The mentor always offers to introduce someone to the group when they arrive a little late.
examples.zh: 有人稍晚一点到时，学长总会主动「把这人介绍给大家」。

collocations: offer to introduce someone to the group
ask a host to introduce someone to the group
remember to introduce someone to the group

words.enDefinition: signals that you and another person have not met before

examples.en: I said, "We haven't met before. I'm Nia from the floor upstairs."
examples.zh: 我说：「我们以前还没见过」。我是楼上的尼娅。

examples.en: My neighbour smiled and said, "We haven't met yet. I just moved in."
examples.zh: 邻居笑着说：「我们还没见过」。我刚搬进来。

collocations: I'm pretty sure we haven't met
we haven't met before
we haven't met in person

words.expression: how do you know each other
words.lemma: how do you know each other
words.enDefinition: asks how two people first became acquainted or connected
acceptedEnVariants: how do you know each other

examples.en: At the first lunch, someone asked, "How do you know each other? Were you roommates last year?"
examples.zh: 第一次一起午餐时，有人问：「你们是怎么认识的」？去年是室友吗？

examples.en: My new flatmate asked, "How do you know each other? I keep seeing you two together."
examples.zh: 新室友问：「你们是怎么认识的」？我老是看到你俩在一起。

collocations: ask how two people know each other
so how do you know each other
how do you know each other again

words.expression: put a face to a name
words.lemma: put a face to a name
words.enDefinition: to learn what someone you know by name looks like
acceptedEnVariants: put a face to a name

examples.en: We'd emailed twice, so it was nice to finally put a face to a name.
examples.zh: 我们发过两次邮件，终于能「把名字和长相对上」了，真好。

examples.en: The video introductions helped me put a face to a name before I moved into housing.
examples.zh: 搬进宿舍前，自我介绍视频帮我「把名字和长相对上」。

collocations: finally put a face to a name
nice to put a face to a name
help put a face to a name

words.enDefinition: asks which name or form of address someone prefers

examples.en: My new neighbour asked, "What should I call you? I don't want to guess."
examples.zh: 新邻居问：「我该怎么称呼你」？我不想乱猜。

examples.en: I said, "What should I call you? The class list has a different name."
examples.zh: 我问：「我该怎么称呼你」？班级名单上写的是另一个名字。

collocations: so what should I call you
what should I call you in class
what should I call you then

words.enDefinition: to be known by an informal name instead of your full name

examples.en: My art class is small, so I usually go by a nickname there.
examples.zh: 我上的美术班人少，所以在班里我一般「用昵称」。

examples.en: I asked her whether she liked to go by a nickname outside class.
examples.zh: 我问她平时在课堂之外是否喜欢「用昵称」。

collocations: go by a nickname at school
prefer to go by a nickname
usually go by a nickname

words.enDefinition: introduces the name a person normally wants others to use

examples.en: My full name is Amara, but I go by Amy during class.
examples.zh: 我的全名是阿玛拉，但在班里我「平时叫」艾米。

examples.en: I go by Lou, which is easier for my new classmates to remember.
examples.zh: 我「平时叫」卢，新同学更容易记住这个称呼。

collocations: I go by my middle name
I go by a shortened name
I usually go by

words.enDefinition: to say someone's name aloud in a particular way

examples.en: I would rather ask how to pronounce someone's name than quietly avoid using it.
examples.zh: 我宁愿问清楚「怎么念对方的名字」，也不愿悄悄避开这个称呼。

examples.en: It takes practice to pronounce someone's name if the sounds are new to you.
examples.zh: 要是那些发音不熟，「念对方的名字」就得练一练。

collocations: learn to pronounce someone's name
know how to pronounce someone's name
pronounce someone's name correctly

words.enDefinition: checks whether something you just said or repeated was correct

examples.en: I repeated her name and asked, "Did I get that right? It's new to me."
examples.zh: 我复述了她的名字，问：「我说对了吗」？这个名字我第一次听。

examples.en: You said your family name comes first. did I get that right, or did I misunderstand?
examples.zh: 你说你的姓在前面，「我说对了吗」，还是我理解错了？

collocations: did I get that right this time
just checking, did I get that right
did I get that right now

words.enDefinition: politely asks someone to repeat a name already given

examples.en: On our second day, I finally asked, "What was your name again? Sorry, I'm terrible with names."
examples.zh: 第二天，我终于问了：「你叫什么来着」？我记人名不太行。

examples.en: What was your name again? I think we were in the same orientation group.
examples.zh: 「你叫什么来着」？我记得咱俩好像在同一个迎新小组。

collocations: sorry, what was your name again
I'm terrible with names, what was your name again
what was your name again, sorry

words.enDefinition: someone you recognise from having seen them before

examples.en: The person by the coffee machine was the only familiar face there.
examples.zh: 咖啡机旁边那个人是现场唯一一个我「眼熟的人」。

examples.en: I spotted a familiar face as I walked into the crowded common room.
examples.zh: 我走进挤满人的公共休息室，看到了一个「眼熟的人」。

collocations: spot a familiar face
see a familiar face in the crowd
look for a familiar face

words.enDefinition: says you recognise someone but cannot remember from where

examples.en: You look familiar. Were you at the welcome dinner last Friday evening?
examples.zh: 「你看起来很眼熟」。上周五晚上你也去迎新晚餐了吗？

examples.en: I told the student, "You look familiar, but I can't place you yet."
examples.zh: 我对那个同学说：「你看起来很眼熟」，不过我还想不起在哪儿见过。

collocations: you look familiar to me
you look familiar, have we met
you look familiar from class

words.enDefinition: asks if you and another person have met previously

examples.en: Have we met before? I remember someone with the same yellow notebook from orientation.
examples.zh: 「我们以前见过吗」？我记得迎新时有个人也拿着这种黄色笔记本。

examples.en: The student asked, "Have we met before? I think we both know Sam."
examples.zh: 那位同学问：「我们以前见过吗」？我记得咱俩都认识山姆。

collocations: have we met before somewhere
have we met before on campus
have we met before at a workshop

words.expression: I think I've seen you around
words.lemma: i think i've seen you around
words.enDefinition: suggests you recognise someone from seeing them nearby before
acceptedEnVariants: I think I've seen you around

examples.en: I think I've seen you around campus, usually at the library around the same time.
examples.zh: 「我好像在学校见过你」，通常是在差不多的时间去图书馆时。

examples.en: The student said, "I think I've seen you around the building, but we've never spoken."
examples.zh: 那位同学说：「我好像在这栋楼附近见过你」，但咱们还没说过话。

collocations: I think I've seen you around campus
I think I've seen you around here
I think I've seen you around the gym

words.enDefinition: to identify a person you have seen in a class

examples.en: It was nice to recognise someone from class when I reached the crowded dining hall.
examples.zh: 进到挤满人的食堂时，能「认出一个上课见过的人」让我很高兴。

examples.en: I thought I might recognise someone from class at the welcome picnic on Friday.
examples.zh: 我想周五迎新野餐时也许能「认出一个上课见过的人」。

collocations: recognise someone from class at lunch
immediately recognise someone from class
recognise someone from class by their voice

words.enDefinition: students at the same stage in their course or schooling

examples.en: Two of the people I met were in the same year group as me.
examples.zh: 我认识的两个人和我在「同一年级」。

examples.en: We shared some lectures because we were in the same year group at college.
examples.zh: 我们在大学读「同一年级」，有几门大课一起上。

collocations: be in the same year group
people in the same year group
friends from the same year group

words.enDefinition: someone who attends the same school or university as you

examples.en: A fellow student helped me find the room for my first seminar.
examples.zh: 一位「同校学生」帮我找到了第一堂研讨课的教室。

examples.en: I met a fellow student who lived in the building across from mine.
examples.zh: 我认识了一位「同校学生」，住在我那栋楼对面。

collocations: talk to a fellow student
ask a fellow student
meet a fellow student

words.enDefinition: students who start or study a program as one group

examples.en: The welcome event was the first time our student cohort met in person.
examples.zh: 那场迎新活动是我们「这批学生」第一次线下见面。

examples.en: She recognised a few people from her student cohort in the dining hall.
examples.zh: 她在食堂认出了几位「同批学生」。

collocations: meet the student cohort
part of the same student cohort
incoming student cohort

words.enDefinition: in British university usage, a student taking the same degree course as you

examples.en: A coursemate recognised me by the badges on my laptop cover.
examples.zh: 一位「同专业同学」认出了我笔记本保护壳上的徽章。

examples.en: My coursemate and I both chose the same optional module this term.
examples.zh: 这学期，我和一位「同专业同学」选了同一门选修课。

collocations: talk to a coursemate
pair up with a coursemate
help a coursemate

words.enDefinition: people who live in the same residence hall as the speaker

examples.en: I saw some people from my hall at the food truck near the library.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆旁边的餐车前看到了几个「我宿舍楼的人」。

examples.en: Two people from my hall turned out to be taking the same history class.
examples.zh: 有两个「我宿舍楼的人」原来也选了同一门历史课。

collocations: meet people from my hall
eat with people from my hall
recognise people from my hall

words.enDefinition: to have a room or home on the same building level

examples.en: We discovered we live on the same floor when we both headed for the stairs.
examples.zh: 我们都往楼梯走时，发现彼此「住在同一层」。

examples.en: Four people in my lab group live on the same floor as I do.
examples.zh: 实验小组里有四个人和我「住在同一层」。

collocations: happen to live on the same floor
both live on the same floor
live on the same floor in residence

words.enDefinition: having only recently arrived at or joined a university community

examples.en: I was new to campus and didn't recognise anyone at the first lunch.
examples.zh: 我「刚来学校」，在第一次午餐时谁都不认识。

examples.en: Several of us were new to campus, so we compared notes about the area.
examples.zh: 我们有好几个人「刚来学校」，于是聊了聊各自对附近的了解。

collocations: be new to campus
still new to campus
students who are new to campus

words.enDefinition: indicating that a person has never visited a place before

examples.en: It's my first time here, so I don't know where everyone usually sits.
examples.zh: 我「第一次来这里」，还不知道大家通常坐哪儿。

examples.en: I told the person beside me that it was my first time here.
examples.zh: 我告诉旁边的人，这是我「第一次来这里」。

collocations: my first time here
realise it is someone's first time here
ask if it's their first time here

words.enDefinition: asks whether someone only recently arrived or joined a place

examples.en: Are you new here, or were you at the first welcome session last week?
examples.zh: 「你是刚来的吗」？还是上周也参加了第一场迎新活动？

examples.en: The person in line asked, "Are you new here? I moved in on Tuesday."
examples.zh: 排队时，一个人问：「你是刚来的吗」？我周二搬进来的。

collocations: are you new here too
are you new here or just visiting
so are you new here

words.enDefinition: to start talking to someone without a prior arrangement

examples.en: I wanted to strike up a conversation with someone while waiting for the bus.
examples.zh: 等公交的时候，我想找个人「主动聊上几句」。

examples.en: It was easy to strike up a conversation because we recognised each other's course books.
examples.zh: 我们认出了彼此的课本，所以很容易就「攀谈起来」。

collocations: strike up a conversation with a stranger
strike up a conversation in line
easy to strike up a conversation

words.enDefinition: to begin talking informally, often without planning to

examples.en: We started comparing our schedules and managed to get chatting before the session.
examples.zh: 我们先是对了对课表，活动开始前就「聊起来」了。

examples.en: It's easy to get chatting with people while waiting outside the seminar room.
examples.zh: 在研讨课的教室外等候时，很容易和人「聊起来」。

collocations: get chatting in the queue
get chatting over coffee
get chatting with someone

words.enDefinition: informal conversation about everyday things of little importance

examples.en: The chitchat before our seminar made the room feel more relaxed.
examples.zh: 研讨课开始前的「闲聊」让教室里的气氛放松了些。

examples.en: We had a bit of chitchat while waiting for the lift.
examples.zh: 等电梯时，我们「闲聊」了几句。

collocations: friendly chitchat
casual chitchat
time for chitchat

words.enDefinition: playful remarks exchanged between people who are joking together

examples.en: The friendly banter made me less nervous about joining the table.
examples.zh: 几句「善意的玩笑话」让我坐过去时没那么紧张了。

examples.en: There was a little banter about whose timetable looked the busiest.
examples.zh: 大家说了几句「善意的玩笑话」，主题是谁的课表看起来最满。

collocations: friendly banter
light-hearted banter
enjoy the banter

words.enDefinition: a comment or question that helps people begin talking

examples.en: The pins on her backpack were a conversation starter at the welcome fair.
examples.zh: 在迎新集市上，她背包上的徽章成了「打开话题的引子」。

examples.en: Asking about local food was a good conversation starter in my group.
examples.zh: 在我们那组，问问附近有什么好吃的，是个「打开话题的好办法」。

collocations: good conversation starter
use a conversation starter
easy conversation starter

words.enDefinition: a brief silence that feels uncomfortable during a conversation

examples.en: There was an awkward pause before I remembered how we had met.
examples.zh: 我想起我们是怎么认识的之前，出现了一阵「尴尬的停顿」。

examples.en: After an awkward pause, I asked what classes everyone was taking.
examples.zh: 出现「尴尬的停顿」后，我问了问大家都选了什么课。

collocations: an awkward pause in conversation
fill an awkward pause
avoid an awkward pause

words.enDefinition: a brief period when people talking together become quiet

examples.en: I used a lull in the conversation to introduce myself to the person beside me.
examples.zh: 我趁着「聊天间隙」向旁边的人做了自我介绍。

examples.en: Someone brought more tea during a lull in the conversation, and we started talking again.
examples.zh: 有人趁着「聊天间隙」又端来些茶，我们就接着聊了。

collocations: a brief lull in the conversation
fill a lull in the conversation
speak during a lull in the conversation

words.enDefinition: a subject unlikely to cause tension or make people uncomfortable

examples.en: The campus bus was a safe topic when nobody knew each other yet.
examples.zh: 大家还不认识的时候，校园公交是个「稳妥的话题」。

examples.en: I went with a safe topic and asked about the new student café.
examples.zh: 我选了个「稳妥的话题」，问起新开的学生咖啡馆。

collocations: choose a safe topic
stick to a safe topic
start with a safe topic

words.enDefinition: to help people keep talking without the exchange ending

examples.en: I asked about the neighborhood to keep the conversation going while we waited outside.
examples.zh: 我们在外面等的时候，我问起附近的情况，好「让聊天继续下去」。

examples.en: A shared interest in old films helped keep the conversation going well after dinner.
examples.zh: 两人都喜欢老电影，所以晚饭结束好一会儿还能「接着聊下去」。

collocations: ask questions to keep the conversation going
try to keep the conversation going
manage to keep the conversation going

words.enDefinition: to do most of the work of keeping people talking

examples.en: At first I had to carry the conversation because everyone was still nervous.
examples.zh: 一开始大家还很紧张，我只好一个人「独力维持聊天」。

examples.en: I relaxed when I realised I didn't have to carry the conversation on my own.
examples.zh: 意识到不用我独自「独力维持聊天」之后，我就放松了。

collocations: feel obliged to carry the conversation
expect someone to carry the conversation
try to carry the conversation

words.enDefinition: to avoid making a conversation serious or uncomfortable

examples.en: I tried to keep it light by asking about her favourite campus lunch.
examples.zh: 我想「保持话题轻松」，就问她喜欢学校哪种午餐。

examples.en: We decided to keep it light while everyone was still getting to know each other.
examples.zh: 大家还在彼此熟悉的阶段，我们决定「保持话题轻松」。

collocations: try to keep it light
keep it light at first
keep it light with a joke

words.enDefinition: to ask one more question based on someone's previous answer

examples.en: I wanted to ask a follow-up after she mentioned the campus radio station.
examples.zh: 她提到校园电台后，我想「接着追问一句」。

examples.en: You can ask a follow-up if their story reminds you of something similar.
examples.zh: 对方的经历让你想起类似的事时，你可以「接着追问一句」。

collocations: remember to ask a follow-up
pause to ask a follow-up
ask a follow-up about the story

words.enDefinition: asks someone's reason for being at a location or event

examples.en: Someone asked, "What brings you here?" while we were waiting for the campus tour.
examples.zh: 我们等校园参观开始时，有人问：「你怎么会来这儿」？

examples.en: I asked my seatmate, "What brings you here? I'm helping with the craft table."
examples.zh: 我问坐在旁边的人：「你怎么会来这儿」？我是来帮忙照看手工摊位的。

collocations: so what brings you here
what brings you here today
ask someone what brings you here

words.enDefinition: asks what subject someone is taking at college or university

examples.en: I asked, "What are you studying?" while we waited for the dining hall to open.
examples.zh: 我们等食堂开门时，我问：「你学什么专业」？

examples.en: What are you studying this year, or are you still choosing between two programs?
examples.zh: 你今年「学什么专业」？还是还在两个专业之间选？

collocations: so what are you studying
what are you studying here
what are you studying at university

words.enDefinition: asks what stage of school or university someone has reached

examples.en: The student beside me asked, "What year are you in? I'm just starting my second."
examples.zh: 旁边的同学问：「你读几年级」？我刚开始读第二年。

examples.en: What year are you in at this university? I think my roommate knows your group.
examples.zh: 你在这所大学「读几年级」？我想我室友认识你们那批同学。

collocations: so what year are you in
what year are you in now
ask what year someone is in

words.expression: what do you do for fun
words.lemma: what do you do for fun
words.enDefinition: asks which activities someone enjoys in their spare time
acceptedEnVariants: what do you do for fun

examples.en: She put down her books and asked, "What do you do for fun after class?"
examples.zh: 她放下书问，下课后「你平时喜欢玩什么」？

examples.en: What do you do for fun on a free afternoon when the weather is good?
examples.zh: 天气好、下午没事的时候，「你平时喜欢玩什么」？

collocations: so what do you do for fun
what do you do for fun around here
ask what someone does for fun

words.enDefinition: to enjoy the same activities or subjects as someone else

examples.en: I didn't expect us to be into the same things after that quiet first meeting.
examples.zh: 第一次见面没说几句话，我没想到我们后来发现「喜欢相同的东西」。

examples.en: It's nice to be into the same things when you're trying to find new friends.
examples.zh: 想认识新朋友时，发现彼此「喜欢相同的东西」挺好的。

collocations: seem to be into the same things
turn out to be into the same things
be into the same things as classmates

words.enDefinition: asks what someone's experience of a place is usually like

examples.en: I asked a student, "What's it like here when most people go home for break?"
examples.zh: 我问一位同学，大部分人放假回家后，「这里怎么样」？

examples.en: What's it like here for new students who don't know anyone in the city?
examples.zh: 对在这个城市谁都不认识的新生来说，「这里怎么样」？

collocations: so what's it like here
what's it like here during term
ask what it's like here

words.enDefinition: asks how comfortable someone is becoming in a new place

examples.en: My new neighbour asked, "How are you settling in after your first week on campus?"
examples.zh: 在学校待了一星期后，新邻居问我：“「你适应得怎么样」？”

examples.en: How are you settling in now that you've moved from the temporary room upstairs?
examples.zh: 从楼上的临时房间搬出来以后，「你适应得怎么样」？

collocations: so how are you settling in
how are you settling in so far
ask how someone is settling in

words.enDefinition: asks how someone's initial week in a new place is going

examples.en: How's your first week going since you moved into the residence hall on Sunday?
examples.zh: 周日搬进宿舍之后，「你第一周过得怎么样」？

examples.en: My lab partner turned around and said, "How's your first week going now classes have started?"
examples.zh: 我的实验搭档转过身问：「你第一周过得怎么样」？课已经开始上了。

collocations: so how's your first week going
how's your first week going so far
ask how someone's first week is going

words.enDefinition: to become comfortable and confident in a new situation

examples.en: It can take a few weeks to find your feet in a new city.
examples.zh: 在一个新城市「逐渐适应下来」可能要花几周。

examples.en: She said meeting people helps you find your feet in your first term.
examples.zh: 她说，结识一些人有助于你在第一学期「逐渐适应下来」。

collocations: start to find your feet
help you find your feet
take time to find your feet

words.enDefinition: indicating that a person is learning how to navigate a place

examples.en: I'm still finding my way around, so I sometimes take the long path to class.
examples.zh: 我「还在熟悉这儿的路」，所以有时会上课绕远。

examples.en: I said I was still finding my way around, and she offered to walk with me.
examples.zh: 我说自己「还在熟悉这儿的路」，她就说陪我一起走。

collocations: I'm still finding my way around
still finding my way around campus
still finding my way around the building

words.enDefinition: to make other people see you in a particular way

examples.en: I worried I might come across as quiet because I didn't say much.
examples.zh: 我没怎么说话，担心「给人的印象是」不爱开口。

examples.en: People who listen carefully can come across as interested without saying very much.
examples.zh: 认真听的人就算话不多，也能「给人的印象是」对话题感兴趣。

collocations: come across as friendly
come across as confident
come across as reserved

words.enDefinition: making others feel comfortable talking to or confiding in you

examples.en: I found my new neighbour easy to talk to even when I paused a lot.
examples.zh: 我经常说到一半停下来，但觉得新邻居还是很「好聊」。

examples.en: The tutor was easy to talk to, so I stayed after class to chat.
examples.zh: 老师很「好聊」，所以我课后留下来聊了会儿。

collocations: find someone easy to talk to
really easy to talk to
seem easy to talk to

words.enDefinition: not inclined to show feelings or share much personal information

examples.en: I was quite reserved until the others started talking about films.
examples.zh: 大家开始聊电影之前，我一直「比较内敛」。

examples.en: She seemed reserved the first day, but we talked for hours later.
examples.zh: 第一天她显得「比较内敛」，但后来我们聊了好几个小时。

collocations: seem reserved at first
quiet and reserved
naturally reserved

words.enDefinition: having a gentle, quiet way of speaking

examples.en: A soft-spoken student asked if I wanted help finding the room.
examples.zh: 一个「说话轻声细语」的同学问我要不要帮忙找教室。

examples.en: My new neighbour is soft-spoken, so I moved closer to hear.
examples.zh: 新邻居「说话声音轻」，于是我走近一点听。

collocations: soft-spoken person
seem soft-spoken
soft-spoken and friendly

words.enDefinition: a person who pays close attention when others speak

examples.en: I realised that my new roommate was a good listener over dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭时，我发现新室友是个「善于倾听的人」。

examples.en: You don't have to talk much to be a good listener here.
examples.zh: 在这里，想当个「善于倾听的人」用不着说很多话。

collocations: be a good listener
find a good listener
known as a good listener

words.enDefinition: someone who moves easily between groups and enjoys meeting people

examples.en: My roommate is a social butterfly and already knows half the floor.
examples.zh: 室友在「各种社交场合都很活跃」，已经认识半层楼的人了。

examples.en: I'm no social butterfly, but I did introduce myself to two people.
examples.zh: 我「在社交场合没那么活跃」，不过还是向两个人做了自我介绍。

collocations: be a social butterfly
known as a social butterfly
quite the social butterfly

words.enDefinition: someone who stays quietly apart from others at social events

examples.en: I felt like a wallflower until her friends waved me over.
examples.zh: 她的朋友招手叫我过去之前，我感觉自己「在聚会上一直独处，没怎么说话」。

examples.en: He was a wallflower at first, then joined the card game.
examples.zh: 他一开始「在聚会上坐在一旁，没怎么说话」，后来加入了牌局。

collocations: feel like a wallflower
shy wallflower
be a wallflower at a party

words.enDefinition: to feel comfortable and free from worry in a situation

examples.en: It helped me feel at ease when she said she was also new.
examples.zh: 她说自己也是新来的，我就「觉得自在」多了。

examples.en: I began to feel at ease once we found a topic we both liked.
examples.zh: 找到双方都喜欢的话题之后，我开始「觉得自在」了。

collocations: help someone feel at ease
start to feel at ease
feel at ease around someone

words.enDefinition: unable to think of anything to say at a particular moment

examples.en: I was briefly at a loss for words after she asked what I liked about campus.
examples.zh: 她问我喜欢学校的哪些地方，我「一时不知道说什么」。

examples.en: We were both at a loss for words until the tutor asked us about our hometowns.
examples.zh: 我们俩都「一时不知道说什么」，直到老师问起我们的家乡。

collocations: be at a loss for words
momentarily at a loss for words
leave someone at a loss for words

words.enDefinition: to begin talking gradually until the exchange feels more natural

examples.en: It was easier to ease into a conversation while we both shelved the books.
examples.zh: 我们一边把书摆上架，一边更容易「慢慢聊开」。

examples.en: I tried to ease into a conversation instead of asking lots of questions immediately.
examples.zh: 我试着「慢慢聊开」，一上来没有连问好几个问题。

collocations: ease into a conversation with a question
help someone ease into a conversation
take time to ease into a conversation

words.enDefinition: to talk about work or study with others in that field

examples.en: My lab partner and I tend to talk shop whenever we meet.
examples.zh: 我和实验搭档每次见面，往往都会「聊本行的事」。

examples.en: Our new friends promised not to talk shop during dinner this time.
examples.zh: 新朋友答应这次吃晚饭时不「聊本行的事」。

collocations: avoid talking shop
tend to talk shop
spend the evening talking shop

words.enDefinition: a joke whose meaning is shared by a particular group

examples.en: I didn't get the in-joke until another student explained the story.
examples.zh: 另一位同学说了来龙去脉，我才听懂那个「圈内人才懂的玩笑」。

examples.en: The mistake on our first worksheet soon became an in-joke among us.
examples.zh: 第一张练习纸上的那个错，很快变成了我们「圈内人才懂的玩笑」。

collocations: share an in-joke
explain an in-joke
turn into an in-joke

words.enDefinition: to be facing the same problem or uncertainty as someone else

examples.en: It's easier to speak up when you be in the same boat as the others.
examples.zh: 知道自己和其他人「处境相同」时，开口就容易些。

examples.en: I felt less nervous when I realised we seemed to be in the same boat.
examples.zh: 发现大家似乎都「处境相同」之后，我就没那么紧张了。

collocations: all be in the same boat
realise you'll be in the same boat
know you will be in the same boat

words.enDefinition: to grow closer through something that two people share

examples.en: We began to bond over our love of cheap science fiction novels.
examples.zh: 两个人因为都爱看便宜的科幻小说而开始「拉近关系」。

examples.en: It's easy to bond over a familiar song when you're far from home.
examples.zh: 在离家很远的地方，人们很容易「因为共同熟悉的歌而拉近关系」。

collocations: bond over a shared interest
bond over a common experience
bond over music

words.enDefinition: an activity or subject that several people enjoy or value

examples.en: A shared interest in photography got us talking outside the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 我们在阶梯教室外聊了起来，因为摄影是我们的「共同爱好」。

examples.en: I asked what shared interest brought the two friends to the club.
examples.zh: 我问是什么「共同爱好」让这两个朋友加入了社团。

collocations: discover a shared interest
bond over a shared interest
talk about a shared interest

words.enDefinition: to share a similar interest, experience, or personal trait

examples.en: It turned out we did have something in common besides taking the same class.
examples.zh: 原来，除了上同一门课，我们也「有共同点」。

examples.en: I asked about volunteering to see if we might have something in common.
examples.zh: 我问对方做过什么志愿活动，想看看我们是不是「有共同点」。

collocations: find that you have something in common
realise you have something in common
discover that you have something in common

words.enDefinition: understanding things in a similar way and communicating easily

examples.en: We were on the same wavelength from the moment we started talking about art.
examples.zh: 从一开口聊艺术起，我们就「很合拍」。

examples.en: After one short conversation, I felt we were on the same wavelength already.
examples.zh: 短短聊了一次，我就感觉和对方「很合拍」。

collocations: be on the same wavelength
feel on the same wavelength
seem on the same wavelength

words.enDefinition: someone with similar interests, attitudes, or feelings to your own

examples.en: I found a kindred spirit in the classmate who loved old maps.
examples.zh: 我发现那个喜欢老地图的同学和我「志趣相投」。

examples.en: She called me a kindred spirit after we compared our reading lists.
examples.zh: 对过各自的书单后，她说我们是「志趣相投的人」。

collocations: find a kindred spirit
recognise a kindred spirit
meet a kindred spirit

words.enDefinition: someone whose character or interests appeal to the speaker

examples.en: Anyone who brings biscuits to a study group is my kind of person.
examples.zh: 愿意带饼干来学习小组的人，都是「和我合得来的人」。

examples.en: I knew she was my kind of person when she laughed at my joke.
examples.zh: 她被我的笑话逗笑时，我就知道她是个「和我合得来的人」。

collocations: definitely my kind of person
seem like my kind of person
turn out to be my kind of person

words.enDefinition: a person whose presence makes a place feel more welcoming

examples.en: There was a friendly face near the door when I arrived alone.
examples.zh: 我一个人到场时，门边有个「让人感到亲切的人」。

examples.en: After a difficult first morning, I was glad to see a friendly face.
examples.zh: 第一天上午不太顺利，见到一个「让人感到亲切的人」，我很开心。

collocations: spot a friendly face
see a friendly face
offer a friendly face to newcomers

words.enDefinition: to feel that others are treating you as part of their group

examples.en: They asked what I thought, and that helped me feel included.
examples.zh: 他们问我怎么看，这让我「感到被接纳」。

examples.en: It's easier to feel included when people remember your name and face.
examples.zh: 别人记得你的名字和长相时，你更容易「感到被接纳」。

collocations: help someone feel included
make newcomers feel included
feel included in the group

words.enDefinition: to behave in a way that puts a newcomer at ease

examples.en: It doesn't take much to make someone feel welcome on their first day here.
examples.zh: 别人在这里的第一天，花一点心思就能「让对方感到受欢迎」。

examples.en: Offering to introduce them can make someone feel welcome when they arrive on their own.
examples.zh: 对方独自到场时，主动帮忙介绍一下，能「让对方感到受欢迎」。

collocations: try to make someone feel welcome
help make someone feel welcome
know how to make someone feel welcome

words.enDefinition: to encourage a quiet person to take part in an ongoing discussion

examples.en: A simple question can draw someone into the conversation without putting them on the spot.
examples.zh: 一个简单的问题能「把人带进话题」，用不着当场给对方压力。

examples.en: Our mentor knew how to draw someone into the conversation by asking about their interests.
examples.zh: 学长知道怎么通过问对方的兴趣「把人带进话题」。

collocations: try to draw someone into the conversation
use a question to draw someone into the conversation
draw someone into the conversation gently

words.enDefinition: to move a chair closer so you can sit nearby

examples.en: Our group was still talking, so I asked her to pull up a chair.
examples.zh: 我们那组还在聊天，我就请她「拉把椅子过来坐」。

examples.en: You can pull up a chair and listen if you don't feel like talking yet.
examples.zh: 如果暂时不想说话，你可以「拉把椅子过来坐」着听。

collocations: tell someone to pull up a chair
invite someone to pull up a chair
pull up a chair beside us

words.expression: do you mind if I join you
words.lemma: do you mind if i join you
words.enDefinition: politely asks to become part of what someone is doing
acceptedEnVariants: do you mind if I join you

examples.en: Do you mind if I join you? I recognised you two from the welcome session this morning.
examples.zh: 「介意我加入吗」？我认出你们是早上参加迎新活动的那两位。

examples.en: She asked, "Do you mind if I join you for lunch? The people I know are in class."
examples.zh: 她问：「介意我加入你们一起吃午饭吗」？我认识的人都在上课。

collocations: do you mind if I join you for lunch
do you mind if I join you here
do you mind if I join you all

words.enDefinition: asks what subject others are discussing at the moment

examples.en: I walked over and asked, "What are you talking about? I heard someone mention the fair."
examples.zh: 我走过去问：「你们在聊什么」？我听见有人提到集市。

examples.en: What are you talking about? I missed the start, but it sounds like something I know.
examples.zh: 「你们在聊什么」？我没听见开头，不过听起来像我知道的事。

collocations: so what are you talking about
what are you talking about over here
ask what people are talking about

words.enDefinition: to add a brief remark to an existing conversation

examples.en: I waited for a pause so I could chip in with my own story.
examples.zh: 我等到话头停了一下，才「插话补充」自己的经历。

examples.en: The student by the window decided to chip in with a comment about housing.
examples.zh: 窗边的同学决定「插话补充」一句，说说住宿。

collocations: chip in with a suggestion
chip in with a question
chip in with a story

words.enDefinition: to do something when it becomes your chance to participate

examples.en: Each of us got to take a turn sharing something about the city.
examples.zh: 大家「轮到自己时」都说了一件和这座城市有关的事。

examples.en: The leader let everyone take a turn so the quieter students could speak.
examples.zh: 带队的同学让大家「轮着说」，这样平时话少的同学也能开口。

collocations: take a turn introducing yourself
wait to take a turn
let everyone take a turn

words.enDefinition: to have fun with others by joking or laughing together

examples.en: We managed to have a laugh about getting lost on our first day.
examples.zh: 聊起第一天迷路的事，我们痛痛快快地「笑了一场」。

examples.en: I was glad we could have a laugh about our matching school bags.
examples.zh: 我们的书包一模一样，还能一起拿这事「开开心心笑一场」，我挺高兴。

collocations: have a laugh with friends
like to have a laugh
stop to have a laugh

words.enDefinition: a student who has just started university in Britain

examples.en: As a fresher in York, I knew nobody in my building.
examples.zh: 我刚在约克上大学，是个「大学新生」，同楼的人一个都不认识。

examples.en: A fresher from Wales helped me find the welcome lunch in Bristol.
examples.zh: 一位来自威尔士的「大学新生」帮我在布里斯托找到了迎新午餐的地点。

collocations: meet another fresher
be a fresher at university
new fresher in halls

words.enDefinition: a student who has already completed the first year

examples.en: An upper-year student at the café told us which buses run late.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆里一位「高年级学生」告诉我们哪几路公交收车晚。

examples.en: I asked an upper-year student how they had met people outside class.
examples.zh: 我问一位「高年级学生」平时怎么在课堂外认识别人的。

collocations: talk to an upper-year student
seek advice from an upper-year student
meet an upper-year student

words.enDefinition: having your home somewhere outside the grounds of the university

examples.en: I was living off campus and wanted to meet other people who commuted.
examples.zh: 我「住在校外」，想认识些也需要通勤来上课的人。

examples.en: Some people living off campus came early so they could introduce themselves before class.
examples.zh: 一些「住在校外」的同学来得早，好在上课前互相认识一下。

collocations: students living off campus
get used to living off campus
experience of living off campus

words.enDefinition: asks where a person lived during childhood

examples.en: She asked, "Where did you grow up? I can hear something familiar in your accent."
examples.zh: 她问：「你在哪儿长大的」？你的口音有点耳熟。

examples.en: I said, "Where did you grow up?" and found out we'd lived near the same river.
examples.zh: 我问：「你在哪儿长大的」？聊了才发现我俩住过的地方都靠同一条河。

collocations: so where did you grow up
where did you grow up originally
ask where someone grew up

words.enDefinition: asks what place someone thinks of as their home

examples.en: Someone asked, "What's home for you?" and I mentioned both cities I'd lived in.
examples.zh: 有人问：「哪里对你来说是家」？我说了自己住过的两个城市。

examples.en: She asked, "What's home for you after you've lived in so many different places?"
examples.zh: 她问：「你住过这么多地方，哪里对你来说是家」？

collocations: so what's home for you
what's home for you these days
ask someone what's home for you

words.enDefinition: asks what influenced a particular choice someone made

examples.en: What made you choose this university when you had offers from two other places?
examples.zh: 你还收到了另外两所学校的录取，「为什么选」这所大学？

examples.en: I asked, "What made you choose art history?" while we were waiting for our coffee.
examples.zh: 等咖啡时，我问：「你为什么选」艺术史？

collocations: what made you choose this university
what made you choose that subject
ask what made you choose the course

words.enDefinition: asks whether someone arrived at this place a long time ago

examples.en: Have you been here long, or are you still getting used to all the buses?
examples.zh: 「你来这里多久了」？还是还在熟悉这儿的公交线路？

examples.en: My neighbour asked, "Have you been here long? I hadn't seen you before Monday."
examples.zh: 邻居问：「你来这里多久了」？周一以前我没见过你。

collocations: so have you been here long
have you been here long or just moved
ask whether someone has been here long

words.enDefinition: says that someone has recently come to live in this place

examples.en: I just moved here from another town and still use the map every day.
examples.zh: 我从外地「刚搬到这儿」，现在还是每天要看地图。

examples.en: Two of us had just moved here and needed directions to the bus stop.
examples.zh: 我们有两个人「刚搬到这儿」，还得问怎么去公交站。

collocations: people who just moved here
tell someone you've just moved here
just moved here from another city

words.enDefinition: attending the same lessons as another person

examples.en: I thought we were in the same class before she mentioned the afternoon section.
examples.zh: 在她提到下午的班以前，我以为我们「在同一个班」。

examples.en: We discovered that we were in the same class when we compared our timetables.
examples.zh: 我们看了下彼此的课表，发现「在同一个班」。

collocations: be in the same class
find out you're in the same class
meet someone in the same class

words.enDefinition: to study the same unit of a university degree

examples.en: I was surprised we could take the same module with such different degree plans.
examples.zh: 我们的修读计划差别很大，居然能「选同一门课」，我很意外。

examples.en: We decided to take the same module after we learned it included field trips.
examples.zh: 听说要出校考察后，我们决定「选同一门课」。

collocations: decide to take the same module
happen to take the same module
plan to take the same module

words.enDefinition: a group of new students assigned to do welcome activities together

examples.en: I recognised her from my orientation group when she sat beside me.
examples.zh: 她坐到我旁边时，我认出她是我「迎新小组」里的同学。

examples.en: Our orientation group had several people who were new to the city.
examples.zh: 我们「迎新小组」里有好几个人是刚来这座城市的。

collocations: be in the same orientation group
meet your orientation group
recognise someone from your orientation group

words.enDefinition: shows that something another person has said also applies to you

examples.en: Me too, actually. I moved here last week and only know my roommate.
examples.zh: 「其实我也一样」。我上周才搬来，只认识室友。

examples.en: I said, "Me too, actually," when she mentioned getting lost on the first day.
examples.zh: 她说第一天迷了路，我说：「其实我也一样」。

collocations: say me too, actually
oh, me too, actually
me too, actually, I thought I was the only one

words.expression: I was just about to say that
words.lemma: i was just about to say that
words.enDefinition: says you were about to make the same point
acceptedEnVariants: I was just about to say that

examples.en: I was just about to say that. Walking through the park is quicker than waiting for that bus.
examples.zh: 「我正想说这句」。穿过公园比等那班公交快。

examples.en: She laughed and said, "I was just about to say that," after I mentioned the loud clocks.
examples.zh: 我提到那几只钟走得很响，她笑着说：「我正想说这句」。

collocations: funny, I was just about to say that
I was just about to say that myself
I was just about to say that as well

words.enDefinition: signals understanding based on a shared or similar experience

examples.en: I know what you mean. My first week was also full of wrong turns and detours.
examples.zh: 「我懂你的意思」。我第一周也总拐错弯、走冤枉路。

examples.en: She said, "I know what you mean," when I described eating lunch alone on Monday.
examples.zh: 我说起周一独自吃午饭，她说：「我懂你的意思」。

collocations: say I know what you mean
I know what you mean about that
I know what you mean there

words.enDefinition: to share a short account of something that happened

examples.en: She decided to tell a quick story about finding her room on the first day.
examples.zh: 她决定「简单讲个小故事」，说说第一天是怎么找到宿舍房间的。

examples.en: We each got to tell a quick story before choosing a new table.
examples.zh: 在换桌之前，我们每个人都「简单讲了个小故事」。

collocations: offer to tell a quick story
tell a quick story about home
ask someone to tell a quick story

words.enDefinition: describes a person who usually does not speak very much

examples.en: I'm not much of a talker in a crowd, but I like talking one on one.
examples.zh: 人多时我「话不多」，不过我喜欢一对一聊天。

examples.en: My new neighbour is not much of a talker until we get onto our favourite books.
examples.zh: 我新邻居一般「话不多」，直到聊起我们喜欢的书。

collocations: I'm not much of a talker
she is not much of a talker at first
turn out to be not much of a talker

words.enDefinition: to become able to remember what the people present are called

examples.en: The name game helped me learn everyone's names before our first lunch together.
examples.zh: 大家第一次一起吃午饭前，名字游戏帮我「记住了所有人的名字」。

examples.en: I need another tutorial to learn everyone's names in my new group.
examples.zh: 我还得再上一次辅导课，才能「记住新小组所有人的名字」。

collocations: try to learn everyone's names
help me learn everyone's names
time to learn everyone's names

words.enDefinition: to form groups with two people in each

examples.en: We had to pair off and tell each other about our hometowns.
examples.zh: 我们得「两两结成一组」，互相说说自己的家乡。

examples.en: The mentor asked us to pair off with someone we didn't know.
examples.zh: 带队的学长让我们找个不认识的人「两两结成一组」。

collocations: ask students to pair off
pair off for introductions
pair off with someone nearby

words.enDefinition: a game of guessing which of three personal statements is false

examples.en: We played two truths and a lie to learn something unexpected about our new neighbours.
examples.zh: 我们玩了「两真一假破冰游戏」，了解了新邻居们不为人知的一面。

examples.en: My group played two truths and a lie while we waited for the pizza delivery.
examples.zh: 等披萨送到的时候，我们组玩了「两真一假破冰游戏」。

collocations: play two truths and a lie
a round of two truths and a lie
use two truths and a lie as an icebreaker

words.enDefinition: to move around and talk to different people at an event

examples.en: There was time to mingle before everyone sat down for dinner.
examples.zh: 大家坐下吃晚饭前，还有时间「四处找人聊天」。

examples.en: The new residents were encouraged to mingle over tea and biscuits.
examples.zh: 组织者鼓励刚入住的人吃饼干喝茶时「四处找人聊天」。

collocations: mingle with new students
chance to mingle
mingle at the welcome event

words.enDefinition: to go around a place visiting several people in succession

examples.en: I wanted to make the rounds before I settled into a long conversation.
examples.zh: 我想先「转一圈逐个打招呼」，然后再找人慢慢聊。

examples.en: We had time to make the rounds and say hello to all three groups.
examples.zh: 我们有时间「转一圈逐个打招呼」，三个小组都问候到了。

collocations: make the rounds at a reception
make the rounds before leaving
take time to make the rounds

words.zhGloss: 只和认识的人待在一起
words.enDefinition: to stay around familiar people instead of meeting new ones
acceptedZhAnswers: 只和认识的人待在一起

examples.en: It's easy to stick with people you know when you're new and the room is crowded.
examples.zh: 刚来时，一屋子都是人，很容易「只和认识的人待在一起」。

examples.en: You can stick with people you know at first while you get used to the group.
examples.zh: 你可以先「和认识的人待在一起」，等适应这个群体再说。

collocations: tend to stick with people you know
feel safer when you stick with people you know
easy to stick with people you know

words.enDefinition: to approach someone in order to begin speaking to them

examples.en: I wasn't sure how to go up to someone at such a crowded event.
examples.zh: 活动人太多，我不知道该怎么「走过去找人攀谈」。

examples.en: It's easier to go up to someone when they are standing on their own.
examples.zh: 对方一个人站着时，「走过去找对方攀谈」会容易些。

collocations: decide to go up to someone
feel able to go up to someone
go up to someone and say hello

words.enDefinition: to become the friend of someone, often someone new or alone

examples.en: My roommate made an effort to befriend the student upstairs.
examples.zh: 室友主动试着「和楼上的同学交朋友」。

examples.en: I wanted to befriend someone who also liked making short films.
examples.zh: 我想「和同样喜欢拍短片的人交朋友」。

collocations: befriend a new student
befriend a neighbour
befriend a classmate

words.enDefinition: to meet people who accept you and share your interests

examples.en: It takes time to find your people when you're new to campus.
examples.zh: 刚来学校时，要花点时间才能「找到志趣相投的人」。

examples.en: The art society might be where you find your people this term.
examples.zh: 这学期你也许会在美术社「找到志趣相投的人」。

collocations: take time to find your people
help you find your people
start to find your people

words.enDefinition: to make an effort to meet people despite feeling shy

examples.en: I had to put yourself out there a little before I met anyone from my course.
examples.zh: 我得稍微「主动去认识别人」，才认识了同专业的同学。

examples.en: It's hard to put yourself out there when you don't know the language well.
examples.zh: 语言还不熟的时候，要「主动去认识别人」挺难的。

collocations: find ways to put yourself out there
hard to put yourself out there
decide to put yourself out there

words.enDefinition: to have no acquaintances at all in a situation

examples.en: It's hard to walk into a room and not know a soul there.
examples.zh: 走进一间屋子，发现「一个人都不认识」，确实不容易。

examples.en: You can arrive and not know a soul, then leave with three new friends.
examples.zh: 你到场时可能「一个人都不认识」，离开时却交到了三个新朋友。

collocations: realise you do not know a soul
arrive and not know a soul
go somewhere and not know a soul

words.expression: have no one to talk to
words.lemma: have no one to talk to
words.enDefinition: to be without anyone available to chat with
acceptedEnVariants: have no one to talk to

examples.en: It's difficult to have no one to talk to during your first lunch on campus.
examples.zh: 在学校第一天吃午餐时「没人可以说话」，挺难受的。

examples.en: I thought I'd have no one to talk to until two new students sat beside me.
examples.zh: 我以为自己会「没人可以说话」，直到两个新同学坐到我旁边。

collocations: feel like you have no one to talk to
realise you have no one to talk to
have no one to talk to at lunch

words.enDefinition: to meet and learn basic things about each other

examples.en: We had a few minutes to get acquainted before our first workshop.
examples.zh: 第一场实训开始前，我们有几分钟「互相认识」。

examples.en: The walking tour helped the new students get acquainted with each other.
examples.zh: 步行参观帮新同学们「开始互相认识」。

collocations: begin to get acquainted
help people get acquainted
use an activity to get acquainted

words.enDefinition: to have a pleasant relationship with someone you know

examples.en: It's nice to be on friendly terms with the people next door already.
examples.zh: 这么快就能和隔壁的人「关系友好」，真不错。

examples.en: I didn't expect to be on friendly terms with so many classmates after one week.
examples.zh: 没想到才过一周，我就能和这么多同学「关系友好」。

collocations: be on friendly terms with neighbours
seem to be on friendly terms
be on friendly terms with everyone

words.enDefinition: to start feeling relaxed when a particular person is nearby

examples.en: It can take a while to get comfortable around someone after a shy introduction.
examples.zh: 拘谨地互相介绍之后，可能要过一阵子才能「和对方相处得自在」。

examples.en: One good conversation helped me get comfortable around someone I had found hard to approach.
examples.zh: 那人一开始让我觉得不好接近，好好聊过一次后，我就能「和对方相处得更自在」了。

collocations: take time to get comfortable around someone
start to get comfortable around someone
manage to get comfortable around someone

words.enDefinition: to spend time among the same groups of people

examples.en: We seem to run in the same circles even though we study different subjects.
examples.zh: 虽然学的是不同专业，我们好像「常接触同一批人」。

examples.en: Two neighbours realised they run in the same circles and knew several of the same people.
examples.zh: 两位邻居发现自己「常接触同一批人」，都认识其中几位。

collocations: tend to run in the same circles
happen to run in the same circles
still run in the same circles

words.enDefinition: a group game that helps people remember one another's names

examples.en: We played a name game while we waited for the others to arrive.
examples.zh: 我们一边等其他人到，一边玩了个「名字破冰游戏」。

examples.en: A name game helped me remember the people sitting on either side.
examples.zh: 一个「名字破冰游戏」帮我记住了坐在两边的人。

collocations: play a name game
start with a name game
simple name game

words.enDefinition: an amusing or unexpected detail about you to share with others

examples.en: The worksheet asked you to include a fun fact about yourself alongside your name.
examples.zh: 练习纸要求你在姓名旁写「关于自己的一件趣事」。

examples.en: It's hard to think of a fun fact about yourself when everyone is listening.
examples.zh: 大家都在听的时候，很难想出「关于自己的一件趣事」。

collocations: share a fun fact about yourself
think of a fun fact about yourself
tell us a fun fact about yourself

words.expression: turn to the person next to you
words.lemma: turn to the person next to you
words.enDefinition: to face the person beside you to speak with them
acceptedEnVariants: turn to the person next to you

examples.en: Before we started the game, she said to turn to the person next to you and introduce yourself.
examples.zh: 游戏开始前，她请大家「转向旁边的人」，做个自我介绍。

examples.en: The leader said, "Turn to the person next to you and ask their name before we begin."
examples.zh: 带队的同学说：「转向你旁边的人」，先问问对方的名字，我们再开始。

collocations: please turn to the person next to you
first turn to the person next to you
turn to the person next to you and say hello

words.enDefinition: to greet someone briefly when you walk past or happen to meet

examples.en: At first we would only say hi in passing on our way to class.
examples.zh: 起初，我们只在去上课途中「碰见时顺口打招呼」。

examples.en: I used to say hi in passing before I learned he lived upstairs.
examples.zh: 还不知道他住楼上时，我过去只是「碰见时顺口打招呼」。

collocations: usually say hi in passing
just say hi in passing
say hi in passing on campus

words.enDefinition: to greet a person by moving your raised hand

examples.en: There was just time to give someone a wave before the next talk began.
examples.zh: 下一场讲座快开始了，只来得及「朝别人挥手打个招呼」。

examples.en: I try to give someone a wave if I recognise them in the crowd.
examples.zh: 在人群里认出对方，我会尽量「朝对方挥手打个招呼」。

collocations: remember to give someone a wave
give someone a wave across the hall
give someone a wave from the doorway

words.enDefinition: a small movement of the head used as a warm greeting

examples.en: She gave me a friendly nod when I walked past her table.
examples.zh: 我从她那桌旁经过时，她「友好地点了点头」。

examples.en: I responded with a friendly nod because the speaker had already started.
examples.zh: 主讲人已经开始讲话，我就「友好地点头」回应。

collocations: give a friendly nod
acknowledge someone with a friendly nod
return a friendly nod

words.enDefinition: to smile at someone who has smiled at you

examples.en: I tried to smile back before I asked if she knew Maya.
examples.zh: 我先试着「回以微笑」，再问她认不认识玛雅。

examples.en: It felt natural to smile back when I recognised her from orientation.
examples.zh: 认出她是迎新时见过的人，我很自然地「回以微笑」。

collocations: remember to smile back
start to smile back
take a moment to smile back

words.enDefinition: to stay behind instead of approaching or taking part right away

examples.en: I decided to hang back until someone introduced me to the group.
examples.zh: 我决定先「留在后面观望」，等有人把我介绍给大家。

examples.en: She chose to hang back at first and watch the others play.
examples.zh: 她决定先「留在后面观望」，看看其他人怎么玩。

collocations: tend to hang back
hang back at first
hang back by the door

words.enDefinition: a discussion between just two people without a group present

examples.en: I felt more relaxed in a one-on-one conversation than in the group.
examples.zh: 「一对一聊天」让我感觉更放松。

examples.en: I had a one-on-one conversation with her while the others were eating.
examples.zh: 其他人吃东西时，我和她「一对一聊了会儿」。

collocations: have a one-on-one conversation
prefer a one-on-one conversation
start a one-on-one conversation

words.enDefinition: invites someone to sit beside or near the speaker's group

examples.en: You can take a seat with us if you don't see anyone from your class.
examples.zh: 要是没看到班里的同学，可以「来跟我们一起坐」。

examples.en: The student by the door said I could take a seat with us if I wanted.
examples.zh: 门边的同学说我要是愿意，可以「来跟我们一起坐」。

collocations: come and take a seat with us
you can take a seat with us
feel free to take a seat with us

words.enDefinition: to give each other your phone numbers

examples.en: We decided to swap numbers after realising we took the same bus.
examples.zh: 发现我们坐同一班公交之后，我们决定「互留电话号码」。

examples.en: Would you like to swap numbers before everyone leaves for the afternoon?
examples.zh: 大家下午散场前，你愿意「互留电话号码」吗？

collocations: ask to swap numbers
agree to swap numbers
want to swap numbers

words.enDefinition: asks what username someone uses on a social media service

examples.en: What's your handle on the student app? I can send you the picture.
examples.zh: 你在学生应用上的「用户名是什么」？我可以把照片发给你。

examples.en: She asked, "What's your handle? I thought I'd seen your drawings online."
examples.zh: 她问：「你的用户名是什么」？我记得我在网上看过你的画。

collocations: so what's your handle
what's your handle on the app
ask what's your handle

words.enDefinition: to connect with your account on a social networking service

examples.en: Can I add you on social media so I can send you the photos later?
examples.zh: 我能「在社交平台加你」吗？这样之后能把照片发给你。

examples.en: I wanted to add you on social media after our chat at the art table.
examples.zh: 在美术摊位聊过之后，我想「在社交平台加你」。

collocations: can I add you on social media
happy to add you on social media
ask before I add you on social media

words.enDefinition: to store your phone number in a device's contacts

examples.en: Let me save your number before my phone runs out of battery again.
examples.zh: 我先「存一下你的号码」，免得手机又没电了。

examples.en: Can I save your number so I know it's you when you call?
examples.zh: 我能「存一下你的号码」吗？你打来时我就知道是你了。

collocations: can I save your number
let me save your number
remember to save your number

words.enDefinition: a casual goodbye suggesting you may meet again nearby

examples.en: I said, "I'll see you around," when we parted at the library steps.
examples.zh: 在图书馆台阶处分开时，我说了声「回头见」。

examples.en: She waved and said, "I'll see you around," before heading to her next class.
examples.zh: 她挥挥手说了声「回头见」，然后去上下一节课了。

collocations: alright, I'll see you around
I guess I'll see you around
I'll see you around campus

words.enDefinition: to find a chance to speak while others are talking

examples.en: Everyone was talking at once, so it was hard to get a word in.
examples.zh: 大家同时开口，很难「插得上话」。

examples.en: I finally managed to get a word in when they stopped to check the map.
examples.zh: 他们停下来查看地图时，我终于「插得上话」了。

collocations: hard to get a word in
finally get a word in
let someone get a word in
